text.p: The following are the main stories from Tuesday morning's Austrian newspapers:

- Employers' and employees' representatives have agreed that heavily discussed work laws on night work and flexible work hours will only be fixed in collective work agreements. Civil servants should work on a more flexible basis and up to 48 hours a week.
- Die Erste savings bank will most probably be part of the consortium around EA-Generali, which is bidding for government sell-off candidate Creditanstalt. However, talks are still continuing.
- Finance Minister Viktor Klima wants to save 10.7 billion schillings by excluding various institutions from the budget.
- Klima says financial and economic ideas presented by Freedom Party leader Joerg Haider at his party convention over the weekend would cost the state at least 180 billion schillings.
- Grocery chain Billa has accused Spar of trying to monopolise the western Austrian supermarket sector by taking over Switzerland's Migros chain familia.
- Sports goods maker HTM has been given an ultimatum by banks to pay back interest worth 190 million schillings by today or face legal action.
- Economics Minister Hannes Farnleitner wants to see more competition in Austria's energy market by reducing regional protectionism.
- Fibre maker Lenzing AG is in talks with Courtauld's Belgian fibre maker over a joint venture in the United States.
- Bank Austria expects an operating profit of five billion schillings this year.
- Raiffeisen Zentralbank is interested in the privatisation of the Czech Republic's banks and is also waiting to get a license in New York.
- Austrian milk and cereal product exports to Italy doubled in the first half of 1996.
